note: Creates a data producer over the entire attacker-controlled input buffer; the producer consumes bytes from the end of the input for parameter generation.
Reads bytes from the end of the input to determine how many trailing bytes are reserved for parameter generation; the remaining leading bytes become the compression source.

code: size_t remaining = producer->size - newSize; producer->data = producer->data + remaining; producer->size = newSize;
note: Advances the producer data pointer past the reserved prefix so that the producer now reads only from the trailing parameter bytes; the leading bytes are returned as the compression source.
The remaining leading bytes of the input become the source data that will be compressed; its size is stored back into size.

Reads parameter bytes from the producer to select a compression strategy between ZSTD_fast (1) and ZSTD_btultra2 (9); selecting strategy 8 (ZSTD_btultra) or 9 (ZSTD_btultra2) yields optLevel >= 1, which is required to reach the vulnerable code path.
Sets a random compression level from the producer bytes; the level influences the targetLength and other parameters that affect the optimal parser's behavior.
Sets a random targetLength from the producer bytes; a small targetLength makes the optimal parser more likely to replace matches and evaluate the vulnerable LIT_PRICE(ip+cur) call.
Builds a dictionary from the source data using parameters from the producer; the dictionary provides the reference data that the compressor matches against.

code: size_t const cSize = compress(cBuf, neededBufSize, src, size, dict.buff, dict.size, producer, refPrefix, dictContentType);
note: Calls the compress function with the attacker-controlled source data and the generated dictionary; this is where the vulnerable compression path is exercised.
Splits the source data into chunks using producer bytes; the chunk size is chosen from the producer so that the final chunk ends near the end of the input buffer.
Selects a compression mode from the producer; mode 3 (ZSTD_e_end) is used to finish the frame and flush the compressor, which triggers the final block compression.
Calls ZSTD_compressStream2 with ZSTD_e_end, which flushes the remaining input and compresses the final block using the selected strategy (btultra or btultra2).
Dispatches to ZSTD_compressBlock_opt2 because the strategy is ZSTD_btultra2 (optLevel=2), which invokes the vulnerable optimal parser.
Enters the main optimal-parser loop; ip is the current position in the input buffer and ilimit = iend - 8, so ip can be at most iend - 9.
Reads the literal length from the optimal parser state; the attacker-controlled input and parameters determine whether litlen is 0, which affects the price calculations.
Checks whether the incremental price of adding one literal is negative; this depends on the entropy table built from the input data and can be true for certain byte distributions.
Checks whether the previous match had zero literal length; when true, the code proceeds to replace the match with a literal, which is the vulnerable path.
Iterates over candidate positions starting at cur=1; last_pos can be large when a long match extends to or beyond the end of the input buffer.
Calls ZSTD_rawLiteralsCost with ip+cur as the pointer; when cur > 8 (since ip < iend-8), ip+cur points beyond the valid input buffer, causing a read of uninitialized memory in ZSTD_rawLiteralsCost.

Reads the first byte at the out-of-bounds pointer ip+cur; this byte is uninitialized memory, and its value is used to compute the literal cost, triggering the use-of-uninitialized-value memory safety violation.
